assertions.subject: Vascular Dementia
assertions.quote: Historically, the incidence of vascular dementia has been believed to increase, more or less linearly, with age.

assertions.subject: Vascular Dementia
assertions.quote: one report with more than 1.4 million person-years of follow-up concluded that cerebrovascular disease is no longer a risk factor for dementia among older adults.

assertions.subject: Vascular Dementia
assertions.predicate: second most common cause of dementia
assertions.quote: consensus traditionally considers vascular dementia the second most common cause of dementia—after AD—in North America and Europe

assertions.subject: Vascular Dementia
assertions.quote: Neuropathologic studies illustrate vascular dementia's high degree of heterogeneity, with multiple and overlapping types of cerebrovascular disease damaging multiple sites in the vascular tree.

assertions.subject: Vascular Dementia
assertions.quote: Estimates are complicated, however, by the prevalence of mixed dementias, often vascular dementia in combination with Alzheimer disease pathology

assertions.subject: Vascular Dementia
assertions.quote: Cardiovascular risk factors for vascular dementia include smoking, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, obesity, and physical inactivity, among others.
